text: Lena is a woman of strong ___ and she keeps her promises.
why: Unnatural singular: normal English is 'strong principles' (or 'a woman of principle').

text: Deep down, his ___ knew the answer was wrong.
why: Conscience is about right and wrong, not about a wrong answer; the sentence is unnatural.

text: A local anaesthetic kept her ___ during the short operation.
why: Bad logic: an anaesthetic does not keep you conscious. Better: 'With a local anaesthetic, she stayed ___'.

text: Is the baby ___ or still asleep?
why: Unnatural: the opposite of asleep is 'awake'; 'conscious' contrasts with 'unconscious'.

text: It is hard to ___ if the fish is fresh.
why: 'It is hard to say if...' is also fully correct.

text: I can always ___ when my sister is nervous.
why: Uses tell = know/recognise, which the hint does not cover; 'say' is marginally possible too.

text: Can you ___ the difference between these two twins?
why: The idiom 'tell the difference' is not covered by the hint; 'these two twins' is also redundant.

text: Nobody should ___ people who are travelling alone.
why: Odd meaning: it implies robbing other people is fine.

text: Mum, can I ___ my friend to the cinema with me?
why: 'bring my friend ... with me' is also natural and widely used.

text: Don't forget to ___ an umbrella when you leave the house.
why: 'bring an umbrella' is very common, especially in American English.

text: I always ___ a sandwich to work in my bag.
why: 'bring a sandwich to work' is equally natural (the speaker is at work when eating it).

text: He asked me to ___ his keys to him at the gym.
why: Both work: 'bring them to him' (towards the listener) or 'take them to him' (away from the speaker).

text: Remember to ___ your phone when you go hiking.
why: 'bring your phone' is also standard, especially in American English.

text: That is a ___ story, but it is not true.
why: 'a fun story' (adjective fun) is also acceptable.

text: I like the ___ parts of the book best.
why: 'the fun parts' is equally natural.

text: Her ___ hat made everybody smile.
why: 'Her fun hat' is also acceptable.

text: She sent me a ___ picture of her cat.
why: 'a fun picture' is also acceptable.

text: The company had ___ difficulties last winter.
why: Unnatural for a company: native speakers say 'financial difficulties'; 'economic' is used for countries and regions.

text: He wrote a kind and ___ letter to his sick friend.
why: 'a kind and sensible letter' also works; sensitive = tactful is not in the hint.

text: Will they ___ the match because of the injury?
why: 'miss the match because of the injury' (players cannot play) is just as natural.

text: She does not ___ to win, but she will try.
why: Unnatural: the normal phrase is 'does not expect to win'.

text: Ten items or ___ at this checkout.
why: 'Ten items or less' is the common real sign wording and is widely accepted with numbers.

text: Drive ___ fast in the rain.
why: Unnatural: people say 'drive more slowly' or 'don't drive so fast'.

text: Authors often ___ books into films.
why: Unnatural: filmmakers or screenwriters adapt books into films, authors rarely do.

text: Let's ___ this idea for our class project.
why: 'adapt this idea for our project' (change it to fit) is also correct.

text: We should ___ the best habits from other countries.
why: 'adapt habits from other countries' (change them to fit) is also plausible.
